answer: A farm must thus either lie, which the yarrow graph proves on replay, or recruit 59 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the canyon registry records each claim and the wharf audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 72% of the attester's bond. That is 4 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
